5. Socio-Didact: Adaptive Observation Mode

Socio-Didact is a coined term for a person who learns the unwritten social rules of a network by watching how people and situations are treated. It does not describe a diagnosis, a special cognitive type, or a superior observer. It is simply a functional mode of learning: notice the local rules, notice when they change, and decide how much to adapt while keeping the intended meaning of what you are trying to say or do.

A Socio-Didact may be quiet, peripheral, or easy to overlook. The useful skill is not control over the group; it is familiarity with the setting. Over time, the observer may learn which behaviors attract attention, which cues signal belonging, where friction tends to appear, and when it is easier to stay unobtrusive. The term describes adaptation to a social environment, not mastery over it.

> **Previous continuation:** [HOLDING_AND_ENERGY.md](HOLDING_AND_ENERGY.md) now defines explicit proposed holding, motion and energy-transfer laws, with separate upper-half context exchange. The material below preserves the earlier scalar draft and source history; its open-role statements and scalar checks are not the current energy formulation. See [README.md](README.md) for the current overview.

**Earlier user correction, 23 October (superseded above):** “the hug is the gravity keeping us standing. while the s is the movement its like how energy is tranferered.” The Hug therefore has the intended role of a holding or constraining influence, compared to gravity; S has the intended role of movement/energy transfer. Treating the Hug itself as a clay container and S only as a transported scalar did not capture that distinction. The earlier internal/external-transfer clarification remains relevant, but it does not select the scalar exchange law T3.
## Current role definitions and mathematical consequences
| Hug | A holding or constraining influence, compared to gravity | Its force/potential/constraint law, direction, source and coupling; literal gravitation has not been established |
| S | Movement, understood through energy transfer | Which flow quantity it measures, its direction and units, and its energy/momentum balance |
| Clay | A material responding within that influence | Its constitutive response and coupling to motion; it is not automatically the Hug itself |
| Memory | History can persist while movement changes | Which state stores history and how it affects subsequent motion; a transfer rate is not automatically stored history |
| Doubling | Separate graded upper-half interaction | Its evolution and coupling to the newly defined flow; the reference region defining “upper” must be explicit |

The corpus's scalar context field will be called **S_c when distinguishing it from the newly intended S**. The source formulas below retain their original symbol S for traceability; there it means S_c, not an already established energy-flow variable. The scalar source law, gradient activation, exchange D2 and boundary law T3 belong to that earlier representation. Their checks remain checks of those formulas only.

Velocity and energy transfer are related but different mathematical quantities. Choosing either as S requires a corresponding law and units; using the same letter does not establish equivalence. In particular, the source's scalar ∇S and its source rate cannot simply be reused for a directional energy flow without defining what those operations now mean. No new gravity or energy equation is selected by this clarification alone.

The original fixed-direction force −σ_r a(q)e_k is not automatically the Hug's gravity-like holding law. A material clamp is also not such a law. Likewise, the proposed geometry G1 represents a candidate material body, not a derived shape of the holding influence. These distinctions prevent the old convenient mechanisms from being carried over under new names.

If S is eventually defined as a transfer rate, that rate and a stored-energy or history state must be recorded separately. A zero reading of transfer would not by itself show that stored energy or history had vanished. The user's analogy motivates these separate roles; it does not supply their physical calibration.

## Source equations retained

SOURCE: S is a signed status/context field over a specified continuous embedding. A is accumulated excess input. Neither is identified by the corpus with clay strain, water concentration, neurological memory, or the static scalar S in the separate reciprocal-scaling example. The utility U in this source law is not automatically a physical energy.

SOURCE above records the earlier scalar meaning S_c and does not override the user's correction. INTENT now assigns the holding role to the Hug and the movement/energy-transfer role to S. In C1–C2, the original S is scalar and u is velocity. Mapping the intended S to u, an energy flux or a separate flow field requires an explicit revision, including the gradient response, units, source and observation law. The electrical comparison from the preceding clarification is not a selection of charge or potential as S.

## Meaning of retained memory
INTENT: do not reset memory when motion stops, an orbit changes, or detection fails. SOURCE: A has no decay term. Negative excess input can nevertheless cancel its signed value.

PROPOSAL: maintain an append-only event record with event ID, time interval, input value, baseline, channel/provenance label and units. It preserves the recorded origins even when their net A is zero. This is a record, not an extra force or a claim about biological inheritance. If distinct parent or neighbor contributions must remain dynamically distinguishable, use separately declared A_r and S_r with an aggregation rule. That is a multiple-field extension, not something one scalar A or S automatically stores.

Diffusion and the proposed exchange can reduce spatial differences while retaining M. They do not preserve every detail. An event record can preserve provenance, but it does not make the PDE invertible. If bounded expression is required later, decide whether the limit belongs in an observation map, an added reservoir/transfer mechanism, or a revised source law. Those choices have different consequences. No cap, forgetting term, resetting rule or reservoir is activated here.
## Field presence and detection

The convention is (∇u)ᵢⱼ=∂uᵢ/∂xⱼ. F is attached to material labels; equivalent implementation uses χ on Ω₀. The elastic energy is W=G(tr(FᵀF)−3)/2 for det F=1. The −GI in M1 is an isotropic pressure convention making the stress-free initial state use P=0. This benchmark is isothermal and sets gravity, surface tension and environmental loading to zero. Those omissions are proposed test conditions; a physical fixture experiment must specify its actual gravitational and environmental loads.

M1 is a **new material hypothesis**, constructed from incompressible neo-Hookean elasticity plus Newtonian viscous stress. The elastic term ∇·[G(B−I)] is an explicit addition to C1. The corpus limit G=0 recovers its Newtonian stress; that limit is a fluid, not a calibrated clay solid. This candidate captures elastic recovery and viscous dissipation but has no plastic yield, permanent creep, hydration or damage mechanism. It is neither derived from the corpus nor equivalent to the previous Burgers element. The continuum kinematics and stress construction follow standard hyperelastic conventions; see [Bower, hyperelastic materials](https://solidmechanics.org/Text/Chapter3_5/Chapter3_5.htm). The particular closure and its application here are proposals.

To retain Burgers as a material alternative, specify its tensor form, objective finite-deformation extension, compressibility, state initialization and dissipation. The earlier scalar GM, GK, ηM and ηK do not uniquely supply these. [COMSOL's linear viscoelasticity reference](https://doc.comsol.com/6.4/doc/com.comsol.help.sme/sme_ug_theory.06.029.html) and [large-strain treatment](https://doc.comsol.com/6.3/doc/com.comsol.help.sme/sme_ug_theory.06.030.html) distinguish those formulations. A finite-strain Burgers model remains OPEN rather than being guessed.

The traction boundary fixes its pressure reference; do not also impose an arbitrary zero-mean pressure. In a separate fully periodic/velocity-prescribed benchmark, a zero-mean pressure gauge is appropriate instead.

Additional divergence-free velocity starts are separate experiments with boundary-compatible construction. The corpus's highlighted initial-field proof must not be imported without its actual formula and boundary compatibility.
### Input and normalized source kernel

This retains unit **current-volume** integral near boundaries and during deformation. A moving, domain-normalized Gaussian is the chosen realization of the unspecified smooth kernel. It is not the earlier angular von Mises kernel. Recompute its normalization using the same physical volume weights as the source integration.

Specify U(t)−U_b by recorded intervals with units. A reproducible continuously differentiable test pulse can be ΔU(t)=U_p sin²[π(t−t_a)/T_p] for t_a<t<t_a+T_p, and zero otherwise, with t_a>0, T_p>0. This pulse is C1 across its endpoints, not C∞. Its retained A after the pulse is γ_U U_p T_p/2. Test reversed signed histories separately. Preserve J=κA with no saturation. Pulse amplitude, duration, baseline and conversion constants are required run inputs, not inferred from the old surrogate's combined rate.
### Field transport with the separate mimetic term

J_F=1 in this candidate. There is no additional u·∇S term in S2: material coordinates already follow the carrier. This is the full tensor transformation, not the old tangent-only approximation. It is the specified movement-to-field feedback: movement changes the spatial transport geometry and the physical gradient while A is not reset.
